evals.prompt: hey can you rename fetch_invoice_rows to load_invoice_rows everywhere in my project? it lives in invoice_service.py (copy of evals/files/invoice_service.py.txt) and a few places call it. the tests need to keep passing.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks for a clean working tree, copies the template if it is missing, runs rename-symbol on a narrow --paths, reads git diff, runs the tests, notes that the comment and the LOG_KEY string keep the old name, and runs rg -n for the old name.
assertions: The agent checks that the working tree is clean before it runs the codemod.
The agent runs rename-symbol with a narrow --paths and then reads git diff.
The agent notes that the comment and the LOG_KEY string keep the old name and runs rg -n for the old name.

evals.prompt: Add a keyword parameter debug with default False to run_migration in src/, and pass debug=False at every existing call site so nothing else changes.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs add-parameter with --default False and --call-value False on a narrow --paths, reads git diff and runs the tests. It says that without --call-value the call sites stay unchanged.
assertions: The agent passes --call-value False so that every call site gains the keyword argument.
The agent states that add-parameter without --call-value leaves the call sites unchanged.
The agent reads git diff after the run and runs the tests before it finishes.

evals.prompt: Remove the dry_run parameter from deploy_release everywhere in src/. Make sure nothing in the project still passes it.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs remove-parameter, warns that positional arguments at call sites are not removed, and audits each call in the diff.
assertions: The agent warns that remove-parameter keeps positional call arguments, so each call needs a check.
The agent audits each call site in git diff for a leftover positional argument before it finishes.
The agent does not claim that remove-parameter cleaned up every call site without reading the diff.

evals.prompt: Rename our connect method on SessionPool to open_session across src/ and tests/. We also use sqlite3 in a few of those files.
evals.expected_output: The agent warns that rename-symbol would also rename sqlite3.connect, narrows --paths to the files that define or use SessionPool, and restores any collateral match with git restore.
assertions: The agent warns that rename-symbol renames sqlite3.connect too, because matching is by name only.
The agent narrows --paths to the files that define or use SessionPool before it runs the codemod.
The agent runs git restore on any file whose diff holds a collateral match and narrows --paths again.

evals.prompt: The codemod stopped with a LibCST parser error after it rewrote two files. What do I do now?
evals.expected_output: The agent runs git restore on the touched paths, fixes or leaves out the file that failed to parse, and reruns the codemod on the remaining paths.
assertions: The agent runs git restore <paths> on the touched paths before it does anything else.
The agent fixes or leaves out the file that failed to parse, then reruns the codemod on the remaining paths.
The agent does not treat the two rewritten files as safe to keep without reading git diff.

evals.prompt: Rename the local variable tmp to buffer inside the parse function in parser.py. Nothing outside that function uses it.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the Edit tool on that one function instead of a codemod, because the change is one function in one file.
assertions: The agent uses the Edit tool for this change instead of running codemod_template.py.
The agent explains that a codemod adds overhead for a single-file, single-function rename.
The agent runs the tests for parser.py after the edit.
